strengths: Clearly identifies and articulates two specific, fundamental obstacles to offline hierarchical RL — unobservable inter-level actions and ill-posedness under policy modifications — providing strong motivation for the proposed framework.

The inverse optimization framing is technically principled and non-trivial; mapping state transitions back to latent high-level actions is a genuine insight rather than a shallow repackaging of existing methods.
Breadth of experimental domains (robotic locomotion, supply chain inventory, dynamic vehicle routing) lends credibility to the claimed generality of the framework.
Strong situating of the work across both RL and optimal control literatures, with citations spanning operations research, robotics, and deep RL communities.
weaknesses: A figure caption ('low-level trajectory data (top left) into a dataset amenable to offline RL...') appears verbatim in the body text — a copy-paste artifact that breaks narrative flow and suggests incomplete editing.

The claim of 'safety guarantees needed for safe, real-world deployment' in the final contribution bullet is stated without qualification; offline RL alone does not provide formal safety guarantees, and this overreach may concern reviewers.
The four-bullet contribution list is formulaic and the last two bullets (design decisions investigation, experiments) are more methodological details than conceptual contributions.
The framing around 'OHIO' is introduced abruptly without sufficient intuition for why inverse optimization specifically is the right tool before the technical exposition.

ai_detection.reasoning: The introduction exhibits broad, multi-threaded citation coverage spanning robotics, operations research, and optimal control, and builds a genuinely layered argument over two pages — atypical of AI-generated text which tends to be shorter and more uniform. The embedded figure-caption artifact mid-paragraph is a characteristic human editing error from LaTeX copy-paste. The four-bullet contribution list is somewhat formulaic, but that pattern is nearly universal in ML venue submissions regardless of authorship.
